headline: Dry and warming every day through Black Friday, with Glendale and the other coastal valleys reaching the upper 70s to mid 80s on Thanksgiving and Friday, some Santa Ana winds Tuesday and Thursday, and coastal flood and high surf alerts at the beaches.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: After a weak overnight storm that left less than half an inch of rain (much less in most places), Monday is dry but cool around Glendale and the rest of the LA basin, with clear skies and light winds. A few showers may linger off the Los Angeles County coast this morning. Low clouds and fog hang over interior San Luis Obispo County and the north-facing slopes of the interior mountains.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Light offshore (Santa Ana) winds develop Tuesday under weak high pressure, likely falling just short of advisory levels, and bring warm, dry weather with highs in the 60s and 70s along the coast and in the coastal valleys, including the Glendale area. A weakening cold front brushes the Central Coast Tuesday night into Wednesday morning with generally a tenth of an inch of rain or less there, while Los Angeles and Ventura counties have less than a 10 percent chance of measurable rain. Most areas warm a bit more on Wednesday as high pressure builds in behind the front.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday look warm and dry under strong high pressure, with highs peaking in the upper 70s to mid 80s for most of the coast and valleys, about 10 degrees cooler inland, and averaging 8–12 degrees above normal. Santa Ana winds return Thursday, possibly reaching low-end advisory levels in a few targeted areas, with local gusts of 40–45 mph possible Thursday morning in the western San Gabriel and Santa Susana mountains. There is a strong signal for a stormier pattern returning around the end of the month into early December, possibly a series of storms, but details are fuzzy.

coast: Beach hazards continue this week. A Coastal Flood Advisory for the Central Coast and Ventura and Los Angeles county beaches runs until 3 AM Wednesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch for the same beaches from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon; a separate Coastal Flood Advisory for the Santa Barbara South Coast and the islands runs until 3 PM Thursday, and a High Surf Advisory covers the Central Coast until 3 PM Thursday. Offshore, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through Tuesday. From Wednesday through Friday, seas reach advisory levels on the outer waters (peaking at 14–18 feet Wednesday, with a 40–60 percent chance of advisory-level winds Wednesday and Thursday) and north of Point Sal (peaking at 11–15 feet Wednesday, 30 percent chance of advisory-level winds); south of Point Conception there is a 50–60 percent chance of advisory-level winds and a 30 percent chance of advisory-level seas Wednesday and Thursday, easing by Friday.
watch_for: Coastal Flood Watch late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon for the Central Coast and Ventura and Los Angeles county beaches.
Santa Ana winds Thursday, possibly reaching low-end advisory levels in spots, with gusts of 40–45 mph in the western San Gabriel and Santa Susana mountains.
A possible return to stormier weather around the end of November into early December.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warming stretch through Black Friday and in a weak midweek front, and see a strong but still blurry signal for stormier weather at the end of the month.
